entries.title: Ambience per building and map: register_building_ambience / register_map_ambience
entries.details:
Room tone is now declared like backgrounds: `AmbienceStorage(fallback, *ambiences)` holds `Ambience(sound, priority=0, *conditions, volume=1.0)` candidates; the highest-priority one whose conditions pass plays.
```python
init 1 python:
    set_current_mod('mymod')
    register_building_ambience("mymod_bar", AmbienceStorage(
        Ambience("audio/bar_quiet.ogg", volume = 0.6),
        Ambience("audio/bar_busy.ogg", 1, TimeCondition(daytime = 7)),
    ))
```
`register_map_ambience(map_key, storage)` does the same for a map. Add to a base place with `get_building_ambience("school_dormitory").add_ambience(Ambience(...))`. Paths with a folder resolve into your mod folder. Register at `init 1` or later (the `audio.` names are init-0 defines). Inside a scene: `play_ambience(sound, volume)` / `stop_ambience()`; `end_event` brings the location's sound back. A building without a registration plays its map's ambience. Level your files to -27 LUFS (true peak <= -1 dBTP) and use `volume` only for intent: 1.0 busy, 0.8 outdoors, 0.6 quiet room.

entries.title: Scenes keep the room tone: begin_event ducks ambience instead of silencing it
entries.details:
`begin_event` still stops the `sound` channel, but ambience now runs on its own channels (`ambience_a`/`ambience_b`, mixer `ambience`) and only drops to 35 % under a scene; `end_event` restores and re-resolves it. Replays play the event location's ambience. If your scene relied on silence, call `stop_ambience()` after `begin_event`.

The base audio files moved from `.mp3` to `.ogg` (`game/audio/empty-room.ogg`, …). `audio.empty_room` and the other `audio.` names are unchanged; a direct `"empty-room.mp3"` still plays through a `config.audio_filename_callback` fallback (it also keeps old saves loading), but switch to the `audio.` name.

entries.title: play_sound(..., loop=True) for room tone is deprecated
entries.details:
`play_sound(sound, loop=False, volume=1.0, fadein=1.0)` stays for one-shot effects (moved from `helper.rpy` to `audio.rpy`, same signature). Looping ambience through it still works but sits on the effects channel, is cut by the next effect and stops when a scene starts. Old:
```python
label mymod_bar ():
    if time.get_daytime() == 7:
        $ play_sound("audio/bar_busy.ogg", True, 1.0, 1.0)
```
New: `register_building_ambience("mymod_bar", AmbienceStorage(...))` at init and drop the call from the label.

entries.title: Asset pack 1.0.3 is out
entries.details:
Paperdoll sprites now use the mood token `surprised` instead of `suprised`. Mods that ship their own paperdoll sprites should rename the token too.

A new asset pack is online. Run `tools/Download Assets.bat` (or `python tools/download_assets.py`) to update `game/images` before testing your mod against the current scripts.

entries.title: Paperdoll mood token renamed: "suprised" → "surprised"
entries.details: The misspelled mood token is gone from every sprite file name and from the scripts. Update `PDAImage(mood = "suprised")` to `mood = "surprised"`, and rename the token in your own paperdoll sprites (e.g. `<char> $ 1 surprised $ follow $.webp`). The old spelling now resolves to no head image.

entries.title: LevelCondition: pass the character as char_obj=
entries.details: `LevelCondition(value, *options, char_obj=None)` takes the character only as a keyword. `LevelCondition("2+", "school")` puts "school" into the options; it only looked right because an unset char_obj falls back to a char_obj in the event kwargs and then to the school. All base gates now use `LevelCondition("2+", char_obj = "school")`; do the same in your mod.

entries.title: Decision menu: documented as a Python call, dialog anchor default
entries.details: `call_custom_menu_with_text(...)` and `call_custom_menu(...)` are Python functions: write `$ call_custom_menu_with_text(...)`, not `call`. Name branch labels in full (`EventEffect("my_event.branch")`). The default `menu_anchor` is `MENU_ANCHOR_DIALOG` (choices right-aligned on top of the dialogue box). Keep at least one choice ungated, otherwise the player is sent back to the map with a dev error.

entries.title: Events can carry their own title (title=)
entries.details: `Event`, `EventComposite`, `EventFragment` and `EventSelect` take `title="…"`, shown in event menus, the journal gallery and the cheat page. An entry for the same id in a names file (`translations.csv`, your mod's `names.csv`) still wins, so a mod can rename a base event. When you move a name to `title=`, delete its CSV line; `python tools/validate_names.py` reports a CSV entry that hides a title.

entries.title: Mod page lists what each mod adds and changes
entries.details: Every register function now records what a mod adds and which base or foreign content it changes. The mod page lists events, situations, collectibles and the rest instead of a bare event count, and flags mods that replace the same thing. Register content through the register functions so it shows up there.

entries.title: Situations can pause and follow the event flag
entries.details: `situation.pause()` / `resume()` (or `situation_manager.pause_situation(key)`) freeze a situation without ending it. `Situation(..., flag = "camp", flag_exclusive = True)` makes a situation follow the global event flag: it pauses while the flag doesn't match. Code that *does* something should check `situation.is_running()`; `state == "active"` is also true while paused.

entries.title: Event flags replace the intro condition
entries.details: One global flag (`set_current_flag(key)` / `get_current_flag()`) decides which events may run. Every event without a `FlagCondition` gets `FlagCondition(None)` and **does not run while any flag is set** (e.g. the intro or a camp). Use `FlagCondition("camp")` for flag-only events and `FlagCondition("camp", exclusive=False)` for both. `IntroCondition` is replaced by `FlagCondition("intro")`; the `override_intro` parameter is removed.

entries.title: Map registry: add buildings and whole new maps
entries.details: `map_manager` holds several maps. Add a location with `register_buildings(Building(...))` and `map_manager.add_building_to_map("school", building_manager.get_building(key))`; build a second map with `map_manager.load_map(Map(...))` and switch the player to it. The building key is the label that runs on click.
